newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares lamed by French election, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: German shares lamed by French election, trade thin.

text.p: German shares fell in thin early dealings on Monday following the surprising left-wing win in the first round of the French parliamentary elections.
The 30-share IBIS DAX, which tracks electronic trade in the blue chip DAX index, was down 17.55 points at 3,604.17 points at 0744 GMT, albeit on markedly thin volumes.
Dealers said activity was limited by Monday's market holiday in the United States and Britain and that no solid trend had emerged in the German share market.
"Political events never have a long-lasting effect on markets," said one dealer. "We're looking for a relaxing day."
The pressure came largely from the futures market, where the June DTB DAX futures contract was down 24 points at 3,609 points.
The slightly weaker dollar, always a negative for export-dependent German firms, was also taking its toll.
Dealers said they expected the DAX to trade in a range of 3,580 points to around 3,620 points during the day.
One trader did not rule out a break into positive territory as the day continued.
"With volumes as low as this, anything can happen. And people always want to be in on the rallies," he said.

Dealers also said there was still widespread talk of the need for a correction from the share market's current lofty heights, but noted that this was only likely to happen if other markets, chiefly Wall Street, led the way.
"As long as Wall Street's closed, we're not really going anywhere," a dealer said.
